\[
E(\alpha, k, \theta, z) = U(\alpha, k, \theta, z) + V(\alpha, z),
\qquad
V = \gamma \sum_{\{m,n\}} \frac{[\alpha_n \ne \alpha_m]}{\operatorname{dist}(m,n)} \, e^{-\beta \lVert z_m - z_n \rVert^2}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(\alpha\): The label of each pixel, object or background
- \(z\): The color of each pixel
- \(k\): Which mixture color each pixel belongs to
- \(\theta\): The two Gaussian mixture models
- \(U, V\): The data term and the smoothness term

z is the color of each pixel and alpha its label, object or background. Each side has a Gaussian mixture model of 5 colors, with the parameters theta. k says which of the 5 colors a pixel belongs to. The data term U is minus the log likelihood of each color under the model of its label. The smoothness term V costs gamma whenever neighbors get different labels. It costs less across a strong color change and between diagonal neighbors. Rother, Kolmogorov and Blake set gamma to 50 and beta from the mean color difference of neighbors. Each round assigns pixels to mixture colors, fits the mixtures, and finds the best labels with a graph cut. Pixels outside the box or marked certain never change.
